text:
Maya: Quick sync — we need to lock the telemetry contract for the zone/geo dashboards before the console PRs land. Key things: latency (p50/p95/p99), success/error counts, cross-region failovers, and traffic-split attribution. Who's on this?

Tom: I can take the runtime side. My Q: do we want per-model metrics or just per-route for dashboards? per-model will blow up cardinality.

Maya: Per-route by default, per-model optional behind a flag. Product wants per-model for a handful of heavy tenants.

Priya: Confirming product needs per-model for top 10 customers only. We can mark that as "high-cardinality opt-in" and keep dashboards defaulting to route-level.

Sanjay: For ingestion: we'll accept Prometheus-style metrics. Proposal: histograms for latency (request_latency_ms_bucket + summary for p50/p95), counters for requests_total, failover_events_total. Labels: region, zone, route, env, split_id, route_policy.

Tom: Example payload we'd emit from the runtime:```
# latency histogram
request_latency_ms_bucket{le=\"10\",region=\"us-east\",zone=\"us-east-1a\",route=\"/v1/generate\",split_id=\"A\"} 123
# counters
requests_total{region=\"us-east\",zone=\"us-east-1a\",route=\"/v1/generate\",status=\"200\"} 98765
failover_events_total{from_region=\"us-east\",to_region=\"us-west\",reason=\"capacity\"} 4
```

Liam: Important: record source route and decision that triggered failover. Add a label: failover_stage (eg, "routing","capacity","healthcheck"). Also include the original latency bucket before failover if available.

Sanjay: Agree on failover_stage. For cross-region counts we should emit both direction labels (from_region/to_region). That lets the dashboard compute net movement.

Maya: Sampling: we can't ship full exemplars for all requests. Suggested approach: emit full histograms for all requests (aggregated), and sample detailed traces at 0.1% for root-cause / latency distribution checks. Thoughts?

Tom: Works for runtime. We'll keep histogram resolution high (1ms up to 30s) via HdrHistogram bins. Exemplars (traces) at 0.1% and an override for customers on Dedicated.

Priya: UX ask: console needs to show traffic-split timeline and an easy way to filter dashboard by split_id and by route_policy. Also want an A/B toggle to compare two split_ids.

Maya: Good call. We'll expose split_id as a first-class filter and allow side-by-side comparison in the dashboard.

Sanjay: Storage/cost: emitting zone-level labels for every metric will increase ingestion. Proposal: default aggregation at region-level for long-term retention, zone-level for 7d hot retention. If customers opt-in for per-model or per-zone long retention we charge extra.

Liam: For SLOs we need consistent sampling windows. We should calculate p95 from distributions in Prometheus/HDR-style histograms server-side to avoid client-side variance.

Tom: Implementation detail: runtime will add labels: region, zone, route, split_id (nullable), route_policy. We'll also add route_bucket for priority batching info (low/normal/high).

Maya: Decision summary so far: 1) Emit histograms for latency + counters for requests/failovers. 2) Labels: region, zone, route, env, split_id, route_policy, route_bucket. 3) Failover emits from_region/to_region + failover_stage. 4) Exemplars/traces sampled at 0.1%, opt-in higher for Dedicated. 5) Retention: zone-level 7d hot, region-level 90d cold.

Priya: Can the dashboard show failover "heatmap" by origin region -> destination? UX will want a matrix and a timeseries.

Liam: Yes. With from_region/to_region counters we can build both. We'll also add a derived metric failover_rate = failover_events_total / requests_total per window.

Maya: @infra-bot can you confirm the ingestion pipeline can tag and rollup by split_id and route_policy without schema churn?

infra-bot: ingest-team noted. We'll accept labels up to 12 cardinal fields. Recommend using split_id as a hashed short id (e.g. s1, s2) to keep cardinality low. Rollups: we can configure daily rollup to region-level.

Sanjay: Action item for runtime: add labels + hdr histogram, exemplar sampling flag, and failover labels. (Owner: Tom, ETA: next week).

Tom: Got it. I'll open a PR with the metric proto + example payloads and a runtime flag for per-model metrics.

Maya: Action item for infra: confirm retention policy and rollups in ingest cluster, add docs for split_id cardinality guidelines. (Owner: Sanjay, ETA: 2 weeks).

Priya: Action item for console/product: mockups for split comparison and failover matrix. (Owner: Priya, ETA: 1 week).

Liam: I'll draft the SLO calculation notes and p95 derivation to link into the dashboard. (Owner: Liam, ETA: 4 days).

Maya: Thanks all. If no objections, I'll publish the contract doc today and link to the PRs.

Tom: No objections from runtime.

Sanjay: No objections from infra.

Liam: +1

Priya: +1

Maya: I'll create the contract doc and tag everyone. End of thread.
